text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The World Bank has provided a low-interest loan of $55 million to help develop Vietnam's rural roads.
-- Plans for an industrial park and deepwater port at the northern end of the Hai Van pass, south of the central city of Hue, has been approved.
-- Saigon Brewery Company's trademark of "333" beer has been valued at $9 million.

-- Two foreign brokerage companies, Dragon Capital of Britain and a Japanese firm, are cooperating with Vietnam on a scheme to sell shares of state-run Vietnamese state-run enterprises to foreigners, an official with the Ho Chi Minh City Service of Industry said.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called on the official Vietnam News Agency to improve its information to be a strong national news centre.
-- Finland has given Vietnam non-refundable aid of $6 million to develop rural areas in the central province of Quang Tri.
-- Fines have been imposed on 217 families which had illegal buildings along the main dyke protecting Hanoi from Red River flooding.
-- Laotian Deputy Prime Minister Bounyang Vorachith arrived in Hanoi on Wednesday for a four-day official visit to strengthen relations between the two countries.
-- Vietnam warned business against "money laundering" by foreign financial organizations which offer loans at preferential rates.
